analysis_steps.goal: Measure integrated radio continuum flux densities (including ALMA 108 GHz) and fit spectral index

method.value: Extract integrated flux density from radio continuum images (MWA, ASKAP, ATCA, ALMA) by summing pixel brightnesses above 5-sigma local background noise within the SNR area (excluding unrelated point sources) using miriad imfit and Findlay (1966) eq. 24. Fit a power-law weighted least-squares model to flux density vs. frequency (excluding ALMA due to missing short spacings), and create a resolved spectral index map from 2100, 5500, and 9000 MHz ATCA images.

analysis_steps.goal: Calculate fractional polarisation, rotation measure, and magnetic field strength

method.value: Compute fractional polarisation maps at 5500 and 9000 MHz (5x5 arcsec^2 beam) using miriad impol. findings_qualitative.value: No 12CO (J=1-0) or dense 12CO (J=2-1) clumps are detected towards the radio continuum shell of E0102.

evidence.quote: We do not detect CO emission towards 1E 0102.2–7219.
Spectral line emission 12 CO (J = 1–0), covered by one of the spectral windows in this dataset, is not detected.

Although several CO clumps are detected within the field of view shown in Fig. 11, we find no dense CO clumps towards the radio continuum shell of E0102, suggesting it is interacting with only the Hi clouds.

findings_qualitative.value: A bridge-like structure at 5500 MHz and a central horizontal bar-like feature at 9000 MHz are detected in the ATCA images.

evidence.quote: The 5500 MHz image reveals a bridge-like structure, seen for the first time in a radio image.
Another interesting feature that we detect exclusively in our 9000 MHz image is a horizontal bridge or bar-like feature in the central region with a measured flux density of 4.3 mJy.

findings_qualitative.value: Radio emission extends beyond the X-ray emission, with [Fe XIV] emission sandwiched between the radio forward shock and X-ray reverse shock.

evidence.quote: as it most likely traces the forward shock while X-ray emission could be a tracer of reverse shocked gas (Gaetz et al. 2000).
Interestingly, we note that the [Fe xiv] emission is sandwiched between radio and X-ray emission (see Fig. 5, right).

findings_qualitative.value: An HI cloud at ~160-180 km/s and a cavity-like structure (~3 times the SNR diameter) at 160.1-168.9 km/s are detected towards E0102.

evidence.quote: We detect an Hi cloud towards this remnant at the velocity range of ∼160–180 km s [−][1] and a cavity-like structure at the velocity of 163.7–167.6 km s [−][1] .
We found a cavity-like structure of Hi, whose size is roughly three times larger than the diameter of the SNR shell.

claims.hypothesis: The 4.3 mJy central bar-like feature detected at 9000 MHz could be a pulsar wind nebula (PWN).
claims.experiment: Measured fractional polarisation towards the central region at 9000 MHz using ATCA Stokes Q, U, and I maps.
claims.result: No significant polarisation is detected towards the central region, with a 9000 MHz upper limit of 4 per cent.
claims.finding: A PWN origin for the central feature is ruled out due to the lack of significant polarisation.

evidence.quote: In the 9000 MHz image we detect a central feature that has a flux density of 4.3 mJy but rule out a pulsar wind nebula origin, due to the lack of significant polarisation towards the central feature with an upper limit of 4 per cent.

We did not detect any significant polarisation towards the bridge-like structure and the central region, with upper limits of 2 and 4 per sent for 5500 and 9000 MHz, respectively. This lack of polarisation argues against a PWN scenario for this emission

claims.hypothesis: SNR E0102 has entered or is entering the Sedov evolutionary phase and is expanding into a homogeneous ambient magnetic field in the north-east.
claims.experiment: Measured the radial compression ratio, magnetic field orientation, rotation measure gradient, equipartition magnetic field, and position on the Sigma-D diagram.
claims.result: The north-east shell shows a tangential magnetic field, an RM gradient (+531 +/- 5 rad m^-2 at centre), a smallest radius of 5.8 pc, and a compression ratio of 3.7; overall equipartition B is 65 +/- 5 uG and Sigma_1GHz = 9.17e-20 W m^-2 Hz^-1 sr^-1 at D ~ 13 pc.
claims.finding: E0102 is in or entering the Sedov phase, with the north-east shell expanding into a homogeneous interstellar magnetic field.

evidence.quote: Using this and the radius, we measure a compression ratio of 3.7, supporting the Sedov phase since our compression ratio estimate is near 4 (Sedov 1959).
Comparison with theoretical intrinsic magnetic field estimates and location on a Σ − _𝐷_ diagram of comparable SNRs are constant with it in or entering its Sadov phase with a high ambient density.

claims.hypothesis: SNR E0102 is interacting with an HI stellar wind bubble rather than dense molecular clouds.
claims.experiment: Mapped the region around E0102 in ASKAP HI (1420.4 MHz) and ALMA 12CO (J=1-0 and J=2-1) line emission and compared with the ATCA 5500 MHz continuum shell.
claims.result: An HI cloud (~160-180 km/s) and cavity-like structure (~3 times the SNR diameter) bound the radio shell, whereas no 12CO (J=1-0) or dense 12CO (J=2-1) clumps are detected towards the radio shell.
claims.finding: E0102 is interacting only with the HI clouds (possibly a wind-blown bubble from its massive progenitor) and not with dense CO clouds.

evidence.quote: We propose a possible scenario that the cavity-like structures in both the spatial distribution and _𝑝_ – _𝑣_ diagram correspond to a wind-blown bubble that was formed by strong stellar winds from a high-mass progenitor of E0102 and is now partially interacting with an inner wall of the Hi cavity.

Although several CO clumps are detected within the field of view shown in Fig. 11, we find no dense CO clumps towards the radio continuum shell of E0102, suggesting it is interacting with only the Hi clouds.

why_this_data.value: Complementary ATCA array configurations (long, mid, short baselines) were used to achieve good uv coverage to image the full extent of E0102; ACA + total power 12CO (J=2-1) was used because spatial filtering is significant in 12-m array data and ACA covers a wider region comparable to the HI dataset.

evidence.quote: Complementary array configurations (Table 1) achieved good _𝑢𝑣_ coverage, including long (6A, 6C, and 6D), mid (1.5C), and short (EW367) baselines, essential to imaging the full extent of E0102.

Since spatial filtering may be significant (see section 3.3 in the ALMA Cycle 8 Technical Handbook of Cortes et al. 2020), the line emission [12] CO (J = 2–1) was obtained with the Atacama Compact Array (ACA, a.k.a. Morita Array) comprising the 7-m ALMA antennas and 12 m total power array

why_this_method.value: Briggs robust = -2 (uniform weighting) and Gaussian uv tapering were chosen after experimenting to best image diffuse emission; electron-only equipartition model (kappa = 0) was used as Urošević et al. (2018) showed it is superior to kappa != 0.

evidence.quote: To best image the diffuse emission emanating from the SNR, we experimented with a range of various values for weighting and tapering. We found Briggs weighting robust parameter of –2 (uniform weighting) the most optimal choice.
Their " _𝜅_ = 0" model assume cosmic rays composed of electrons only. Urošević et al. (2018) showed the latter type of equipartition is superior to the former.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Extended configuration ALMA 3 mm continuum observations were available in the archive but excluded because no continuum was detected at higher resolution.

evidence.quote: were available in the archive but since no continuum was detected at higher resolution, they were not included.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: ALMA 108000 MHz flux density was excluded from the spectral index power-law fit because it is affected by missing short spacings.

evidence.quote: We did not use ALMA flux in the fit as it is affected from missing short spacings.

limitations_admitted.value: Limited sensitivity at 9000 MHz prevents conclusively deducing the true nature of the central horizontal bar-like feature.

evidence.quote: We are unable to conclusively deduce its true nature due to the limited sensitivity of our images at 9000 MHz.

limitations_admitted.value: Internal SMC rotation measure contribution is unclear due to lack of background polarised sources near E0102.

evidence.quote: Contributions from inside the SMC are not clear as the latest study of the SMC’s internal magnetic field structure (Livingston et al. 2022) did not have any samples in the area around E0102.

limitations_admitted.value: Uncertainty in the RM-derived magnetic field strength is undetermined because the post-shock electron density uncertainty is unquantified; equipartition is only an order-of-magnitude analytical estimate.

evidence.quote: This approach is a purely analytical method, described as an order of magnitude estimate because of errors in determination of distance, angular diameter, spectral index, a filling factor, and flux density

The uncertainty in magnetic field strength remains undetermined, primarily due to it being a combination of the uncertainties associated with the _RM_ and electron density, with the electron density’s uncertainty being unquantified.

limitations_admitted.value: Higher angular resolution HI observations are needed to draw definitive conclusions about the wind-blown bubble scenario.

evidence.quote: However, more data are required to draw definitive conclusions regarding this scenario, in particular, further Hi observations at higher angular resolutions.

referee_caveats_inferred: The ALMA 3 mm continuum RMS is printed as '31 um' in Section 2.6, an obvious typographical error for 31 uJy/beam.
The ALMA 108 GHz image has a maximum recoverable scale of ~16 arcsec whereas the SNR diameter is ~43 arcsec, causing severe spatial filtering of the 9 mJy flux measurement.
Rotation measure is derived from only two frequencies (5500 and 9000 MHz), leaving potential n-pi ambiguity and non-linear Faraday depth effects unaddressed.
In Section 3.1.1, an average X-ray radius of 20.5 arcsec at 60 kpc corresponds to 6.0 pc, but is miscalculated as 5.1 pc in the text.
